common_rule: Attack the exact registered target. A direction is a starting point, not an assumption; change direction if justified. Deliver concrete mathematics or an exact eligible counterexample, not a literature list. No majority voting. Each new claim is proposed only; no authoritative status.

routes.T1: Direct global deficit budget: double-count or switch across all original favorable leaf tags; permit compensation across supports. Never require refuted pointwise or support-fibre signs.
routes.T2: Induction, pruning, grafting and minimal-counterexample structure. Track first descent and changes in the fixed favorable selector explicitly; seek a closure lemma with fully stated hypotheses.
routes.T3: Matching, minimum vertex covers, alternating paths and bipartite decomposition. Seek complete-sum resource accounting, not universal Hall cuts already refuted.
routes.T4: Probability and hard-core occupancy: rewrite the uniform fixed-rank tagged measure; test a correlation or conditional expectation inequality that implies the budget. Do not assume universal negative correlation.
routes.T5: Rooted independence-polynomial recurrences, transfer matrices and potentials. Seek an inductive state containing enough information to preserve the selector and rank eligibility.
routes.T6: Algebraic or topological methods: graded independence complexes, linear rank maps, discrete Morse matchings or homology. Translate any analogy into an explicit checkable map or inequality with correct hypotheses.
routes.F1: Adversarial multi-hub families around order91 T_22 and order243 T_60: perturb branch sizes and mark counts, evaluate the complete eligible aggregate, never only a positive summand.
routes.F2: Bounded exact asymmetric rooted-gadget search. Use reproducible seeds/bounds, exact integer DP, check original tree alpha, strict first descent, all favorable leaves and strict lower-region guard.
routes.F3: Selector instability: can grafting remove negative favorable fibres while retaining positive ones and both rank guards? Seek a realizable exact positive full aggregate or a sharp obstruction.
routes.F4: Symbolic, tropical and asymptotic constructions: parameterized branch families, subdivision and phase competition. Any asymptotic sign claim must become rigorously bounded coefficients or an explicit finite witness.
routes.F5: Stress-test global deficit relaxations using linear-programming duality or extremal profiles. Distinguish abstract feasible arrays from realizable ordinary trees; only a realizable eligible tree refutes the target.
routes.F6: Cover/matching-controlled trees, path padding and forest-product attachments. Search for eligible sign reversals while explicitly preserving connectedness and original leaf multiplicities.
routes.U1: Audit exact incidence identity, boundary cases and equality/slack. Find the strongest useful exact reformulation of the required global budget, keeping multiply-marked sets counted once.
routes.U2: Minimal hypotheses and minimal-positive-witness structure. Determine what a counterexample must contain and which reductions preserve x,p,alpha and the selector; no unsupported no-recovery premise.
routes.U3: Fractional transport, LP duality, polymatroids and flows. Formulate a global weighted matching relaxation and identify an exact dual obstruction with tree-realizability requirements.
routes.U4: Generating functions, differential operators, spectral or statistical-mechanics reformulation. Identify precisely which coefficient inequality would suffice and whether existing theorem hypotheses are available.
routes.U5: Discharging on support cores and pendant-path compression. Use only the exact sufficient-class scope of r28; investigate compensation between starved hubs and distant leaves.
routes.U6: Finite-state compression and obstruction kernels. Seek a provably sound reduction of possible positive witnesses to finitely many local profiles; distinguish bounded census from universal coverage.
